name: Iron

overview.whyImportant: Iron is essential for chlorophyll synthesis and electron transport in photosynthesis/respiration. Deficiency (iron chlorosis) is very common on calcareous/high-pH soils of India and shows as bright interveinal yellowing of the newest leaves with sharp green veins.

plantFunctions.roleInsidePlant: Cofactor in chlorophyll synthesis, cytochromes, and redox enzymes.
plantFunctions.photosynthesis: Essential for chlorophyll formation and electron transport.
plantFunctions.chlorophyllFormation: Directly required (though not part of the molecule).
plantFunctions.yieldContribution: Sustains photosynthesis in new growth; chlorosis cuts yield.

whyDeficiencyHappens.why: Fe converts to insoluble ferric hydroxide — the #1 cause of lime-induced iron chlorosis.
Rarely deficient in acid soils (Fe more available); may be toxic instead.
Low available Fe, high free lime.
In aerobic uplands, poor aeration reduces uptake; in rice reverse (Fe toxicity).
Bicarbonate in irrigation water immobilises Fe (bicarbonate-induced chlorosis).
Fewer natural chelating agents to keep Fe soluble.

whyDeficiencyHappens.condition: Nutrient imbalance / excess P, Zn, Mn, Cu
whyDeficiencyHappens.why: High P and heavy-metal micronutrients antagonise Fe uptake.
High P precipitates Fe and induces chlorosis — common in over-DAP fields.
Fe immobile; poor roots can't acquire it.
Slows root activity and Fe uptake — early-season chlorosis.
High pH and Na worsen Fe availability.
Using plain FeSO4 on alkaline soil (quickly fixed) instead of chelated Fe; over-P.

symptoms.note: Fe is IMMOBILE — deficiency on the YOUNGEST leaves. Signature: interveinal yellowing with fine green vein network; severe = whole young leaf white.
symptoms.early: Newest leaves pale-green with fine green veins.
symptoms.middle: Bright interveinal yellowing of young leaves, veins remain green (fine net pattern).
symptoms.severe: Young leaves turn whitish/ivory, margins scorch, growing point weak.
symptoms.youngLeaves: First and worst: interveinal chlorosis to near-white with a fine green vein reticulation.
symptoms.wholePlant: Green lower canopy but bright-yellow/white top — the tell-tale top-down chlorosis.

cropWiseSymptoms.symptoms: In AEROBIC/DSR & calcareous soils, young-leaf interveinal yellowing; note flooded rice more often has Fe TOXICITY (bronzing) instead.
Classic iron-deficiency chlorosis (IDC) — bright yellow young leaves, green veins, on calcareous soils.
Young-leaf interveinal yellowing to white on calcareous soils; a major groundnut disorder.
Young leaves yellow with green veins, especially on high-pH/over-P soils.
Interveinal chlorosis of new leaves in high-pH water/fertigation.
Young-leaf interveinal yellowing on calcareous soils.
Bright interveinal chlorosis of young leaves, common with bicarbonate irrigation water.
New-leaf yellowing with green veins on high-pH soils.
Interveinal striping of young leaves (parallel yellow-green stripes) on calcareous soils.
Young-leaf interveinal chlorosis/striping on calcareous sandy soils.
Bright young-leaf chlorosis, green veins, on high-pH soils.
Young-leaf interveinal yellowing on calcareous soils.
Young/top-leaf interveinal yellowing to white streaking on calcareous soils.

howToFix.soilApplicationDose: 10 kg/acre (often with FYM/organic acid; soil-applied Fe is quickly fixed on alkaline soils)
howToFix.foliarSprayDose: 0.5-1% (5-10 g/L), often + 0.1% citric acid to keep Fe soluble
howToFix.methodOfApplication: FOLIAR is far more effective than soil on alkaline soils; repeat sprays
howToFix.precautions: Add citric acid to stop Fe oxidising; soil FeSO4 alone is inefficient on calcareous soils.

howToFix.bestCropStage: On symptoms; the go-to for calcareous soils
howToFix.methodOfApplication: Soil/fertigation — Fe-EDDHA stays available at high pH (Fe-EDTA does not)
howToFix.precautions: Use EDDHA (not EDTA) on calcareous soils; costlier but works where FeSO4 fails.

howToFix.fertilizer: Chelated Iron (Fe-EDTA) — for neutral/slightly acid soils
howToFix.precautions: EDTA unstable above pH 6.5 — don't use on calcareous soils.

methodOfApplication.broadcast: Soil FeSO4 largely inefficient on alkaline soils (rapid fixation); use with FYM.
methodOfApplication.foliarSpray: BEST for quick correction — 0.5-1% FeSO4 + citric acid, repeat; direct to young leaves.
methodOfApplication.dripFertigation: Fe-EDDHA (high pH) or Fe-EDTA (neutral) through drip.

toxicity.whatHappens: Fe toxicity mainly in FLOODED/acid soils (rice) — bronzing.
toxicity.plantToxicitySymptoms: In rice, bronze/orange spotting of leaves (Fe toxicity) in acid submerged soils; stunted roots.
toxicity.correctionMethods: Improve drainage/aeration, avoid continuous submergence, add K/P, lime acid soils, use tolerant varieties.

prevention: On calcareous soils, use Fe-EDDHA chelate, not plain FeSO4.
Correct high-pH irrigation water (bicarbonate) or acidify.
Build organic matter — natural chelation keeps Fe available.
Foliar Fe preventively on chlorosis-prone crops/soils.
Improve drainage in rice to prevent Fe toxicity.
Keep soil moisture adequate for uptake.
commonFarmerMistakes: Using plain FeSO4 on calcareous soil — it fixes fast and fails; needs Fe-EDDHA or foliar.
Confusing Fe (young leaves) with Mg (old leaves) chlorosis.
Over-P inducing iron chlorosis, then adding more P.
Using Fe-EDTA on high-pH soils where it's unstable.
Irrigating with high-bicarbonate water without correction.
Soil-applying Fe without organic matter/acid — wasted.
Foliar FeSO4 without citric acid (Fe oxidises on leaf).
Continuous submergence in rice causing Fe toxicity.
Ignoring tolerant varieties for IDC-prone soybean/groundnut.
Diagnosing Fe chlorosis as a disease.
Expecting old leaves to green up (only new leaves respond).
expertTips: On calcareous/high-pH soils, Fe-EDDHA is the only reliable soil chelate.
For fast rescue, foliar 0.5-1% FeSO4 + 0.1% citric acid on young leaves.
Diagnose Fe by YOUNGEST-leaf interveinal chlorosis with a fine green vein net.
Fix bicarbonate irrigation water (acidify) to stop recurring chlorosis.
Cut excess P — it precipitates Fe.
Repeat foliar Fe 2-3 times; one spray rarely enough.
Use IDC-tolerant soybean/groundnut varieties on calcareous soils.
Build organic matter for natural Fe chelation.
Don't use Fe-EDTA above pH 6.5 (unstable).
In rice, prevent Fe toxicity by aeration/drainage, not more Fe.
Balance micronutrients — excess Zn/Mn/Cu blocks Fe.
New leaves respond; old ones won't re-green — judge success on fresh growth.
Add citric acid to FeSO4 sprays to keep Fe reduced/available.
Combine soil chelate + foliar for stubborn chlorosis.
Keep soil moist for Fe uptake.
Test soil AND water pH/bicarbonate before treatment.
Spray Fe in cool hours to reduce leaf scorch.
Avoid mixing Fe with high-P foliar (precipitation).
Monitor top canopy for the earliest Fe signs.
Log recurring chlorosis fields for a permanent chelate/water-fix plan.

faq.q: Sabse upar ki nayi patti pili, nasein hari — kya?
faq.a: Iron ki kami. 0.5-1% FeSO4 + citric acid chhidkein; calcareous mitti me Fe-EDDHA chelate use karein.

faq.q: Fe aur Mg deficiency me farak?
faq.a: Fe = sabse nayi (upar) patti; Mg = purani (neeche) patti. Dono interveinal, umar se pehchaan.

faq.q: FeSO4 soil me daala, fayda nahi — kyun?
faq.a: Calcareous/high-pH mitti me FeSO4 turant fix ho jata hai. Foliar karein ya Fe-EDDHA chelate dein.
High-pH (calcareous) mitti me Fe-EDDHA sthir; Fe-EDTA sirf neutral/acidic mitti me kaam karta hai.

faq.q: Foliar Fe me citric acid kyun?
faq.a: Fe ko oxidise hone se rokta hai, patti par available rakhta hai.
Haan — zyada P, Fe ko precipitate karta hai. P kam karein.
High-bicarbonate paani Fe ko lock karta hai — paani acidify karein.
2-3 baar, 7-10 din ke antaral par.
Acidic flooded mitti me bronzing — drainage/aeration se theek, aur Fe mat daalein.
Calcareous mitti par bright yellow nayi patti — tolerant variety + Fe-EDDHA/foliar.
Haan, purani nahi badlegi; success nayi patti se judge karein.
Nahi — nutrient disorder; fungicide bekaar.
Alkaline mitti me foliar/Fe-EDDHA; neutral me Fe-EDTA/FeSO4 bhi.
Foliar 5-10 din me nayi patti hari.
Natural chelation se Fe available rehta hai.
Nayi patti par parallel yellow-green stripes = Fe (calcareous soil).

faq.q: Fe ko P ke saath spray?
faq.a: Nahi — precipitate ho jata hai.
Zyada Zn/Mn/Cu Fe uptake block karte hain.
Nami chahiye — dry soil me uptake ruk jata hai.
Us khet ke liye permanent Fe-EDDHA + water-fix plan banayein.
